artifact.self_contained_problem:
For each positive integer $n$, define
$$a_n := \frac{1}{2n(2n+1)\binom{2n}{n}} \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} (10k+1)\,\binom{4k}{k,k,k,k}\,12^{4(n-1-k)},$$
where $\binom{4k}{k,k,k,k} = (4k)!/(k!)^4$ is the multinomial coefficient.

Prove or disprove the following three assertions.

(i) For every integer $n > 1$, the number $a_n$ is an integer, except when $2n+1$ is a power of $3$, in which case $3a_n \in \mathbb{Z}$ but $3a_n \notin 3\mathbb{Z}$ (equivalently, $a_n$ has $3$-adic valuation exactly $-1$).

(ii) For every prime $p > 3$ and every positive integer $a$,
$$p^a \sum_{k=0}^{p^a - 1} \frac{10k+1}{12^{4k}} \binom{4k}{k,k,k,k} \equiv \left(\frac{-2}{p^a}\right) - \left(\frac{-2}{p^{a-1}}\right) \cdot \frac{p^2}{48} E_{p-3}(1) \pmod{p^3},$$
where $\left(\frac{\cdot}{\cdot}\right)$ denotes the Jacobi symbol (with the convention $\left(\frac{-2}{p^0}\right) = 1$) and $E_n(x)$ is the Euler polynomial.

(iii) For every prime $p > 3$,
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1} \frac{1}{12^{4k}} \binom{4k}{k,k,k,k} \equiv \begin{cases} 4x^2 - 2p \pmod{p^2} & \text{if } p \equiv 1, 9, 11, 19 \pmod{40} \text{ and } p = x^2 + 10y^2,\\ 2p - 8x^2 \pmod{p^2} & \text{if } p \equiv 7, 13, 23, 37 \pmod{40} \text{ and } p = 2x^2 + 5y^2,\\ 0 \pmod{p^2} & \text{if } \left(\frac{-10}{p}\right) = -1, \text{ i.e., } p \equiv 3, 17, 21, 27, 29, 31, 33, 39 \pmod{40}, \end{cases}$$
with $x, y \in \mathbb{Z}$ in the first two cases.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not turn up a direct proof or disproof of this specific conjecture (involving the multinomial $\binom{4k}{k,k,k,k}/12^{4k}$ with the linear factor $10k+1$ and the modulus structure tied to $-10$). Many of Z.-W. Sun's supercongruence conjectures have been resolved individually in recent years (often via WZ pairs or $q$-microscope techniques), but no source clearly identifies this particular three-part conjecture as fully proved.

status_evidence.title: On a supercongruence conjecture of Z.-W. Sun
status_evidence.snippet: Paper proving one of Sun's supercongruence conjectures, indicating that many such conjectures remain individually open until specifically attacked.
status_evidence.claim: Recent literature continues to prove individual Sun supercongruence conjectures one at a time; no general resolution of all of Sun's A-series conjectures.

status_evidence.title: A Generalized Supercongruence of Z.-W. Sun
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2026) work generalizing one of Sun's supercongruences.
status_evidence.claim: Active recent research on Sun-type supercongruences; no specific reference resolves the $(10k+1)\binom{4k}{k,k,k,k}/12^{4k}$ family in full.
